rootCauses.title: No single source of truth for the domain model
rootCauses.statement: Three artifacts describe what an order_id means, and they disagree. The producer mints a fresh uuid4 per event (immutable fact). The e2e fixture publishes one order_id twice with different payloads and asserts the later one wins (mutable entity). The PostgreSQL serving schema declares order_id a PRIMARY KEY and updates customer, amount, country and status on conflict (mutable entity). Two of the three say mutable; the running data source says immutable.

evidence.description: fresh uuid4 per event; no order_id ever recurs
dup-1/2/3 published twice with different customer, amount and status
on conflict (order_id) do update set customer, amount, country, status - DDL-level declaration that an order mutates

rootCauses.title: Progress state is an architectural responsibility that no component holds
rootCauses.statement: Bronze carries no row-level provenance, so no delta can be derived from the data. The three units maintain three mutually invisible progress models, and the medallion has none at all. The one existing progress artifact, the writer state file, is unbounded and non-atomically written.

evidence.description: bronze schema: ten fields, no ingestion timestamp and no load identifier
save_state serialises the entire done set on every call, via a truncating write

rootCauses.title: Bronze was never established as a trustworthy log
rootCauses.statement: The Landing-to-Bronze boundary has no commit contract: the writer substitutes a five-second mtime heuristic for Spark's streaming commit manifest, and guards against the wrong protocol's marker. Bronze can additionally gain duplicates from writer re-append when snapshot retention outruns recovery. Neither path is detectable today because the medallion full rebuild silently absorbs both.
rootCauses.note: This is NOT one of the four decisions. It is a defect that exists independently of the incremental question and would remain after any of the six options is chosen.

evidence.description: file eligibility by extension, /_temporary/ exclusion and mtime age; _spark_metadata is never consulted
hourly expire_snapshots on bronze.orders with a 1h retention threshold

rootCauses.title: Full overwrite is load-bearing for three distinct properties, not one
rootCauses.statement: IR-002 as originally stated, that full overwrite substitutes for progress state, is confirmed and understated. It also substitutes for the ordering semantics of AR-004 (recomputing a global max makes late lower-offset duplicates harmless) and for a silver-to-gold data-plane edge that does not exist (gold is computed from an in-memory frame). It is additionally repairing RC-3's duplicates on every cycle.

evidence.description: bronze.scan().to_arrow() - unfiltered, unordered, nothing carried between cycles
build_gold(silver_df) reads the in-memory frame, never the silver table

rootCauses.title: No architectural rule in this system is executable
rootCauses.statement: Sixty tests, all behavioural. Not one asserts an ownership, direction, retention, ordering or reconciliation property. Import-plane guards are unavailable because the single internal import edge is constructed by runtime sys.path mutation. No live-stack test blocks a pull request. Every fixture is single-partition, so no test could exercise partition-scoped behaviour even if one existed.

evidence.command: enumeration of 60 test functions across tests/

decisions.auditPosition: No. Rebuild Gold in full from persisted Silver on every cycle.
